_what: [CORPUS-BASELINE] Corpus checks that already fail, so scheduled CI can report them without blocking merges. This is a RATCHET, not an excuse list.
_rules: Every entry names a tracked issue. No entry without one.
Adding an entry is admitting a defect shipped. Fixing it and deleting the entry is the only correct exit.
Anything NOT listed here fails CI even in baseline mode — that is the regression gate.
`make test-corpus` locally ignores this file entirely and fails on everything. Local runs stay honest.
Check ids are rank-independent on purpose: #301 moves cluster ranks between runs, so a rank-bearing key would churn.

_checks.recall: A hand-verified duplicate was not reported (false negative).
_checks.recall_quality: [CORPUS-RECALL] A hand-verified byte-identical duplicate in `must_find` was reported, but not as what it is: demoted below the `identical` bucket, missing a shown occurrence, or ranked past the entry's `max_rank` ceiling. `recall` sees only whether some cluster spans the paths. The pair must also be classified `identical` by the engine's own verdict, obtained through `deslop --compare`: `must_find` is verified byte-for-byte, so anything looser is the engine contradicting a proven fact about the source, and a missing verdict fails rather than passing (gh #488).
_checks.precision: [CORPUS-PRECISION-CURATED] A pair a human confirmed is NOT duplication was shown as one cluster - a false positive on curated ground truth. Hidden clusters do not breach an entry: precision is what the report shows.
_checks.boilerplate_rank: Framework-mandated scaffolding ranked in the top N.
_checks.data_table_rank: A table of literals is visible in the ranked head. A repeated data structure is not extractable logic - no shared control flow, nothing to hoist - so the noise filters ([CLONE-NOISE-CONSTANT-TABLE], [CLONE-NOISE-DART-DATA-TABLE-LITERAL]) drop it; one still in the head means a filter missed it and it outranks real clones. The verdict is read from the occurrence's AST - a collection whose every element is a literal, or a run of declarations whose every value is one - never from characters of raw source text, and a span that calls anything is code however many literals it holds (gh #452). The old rule counted digits and separator punctuation, scoring a table of string literals 0.00 and ordinary logic under a version-matrix comment 0.74. Its `category != data` clause is gone too: the mass-only wire forbids `category` on a cluster, so it was always absent and the comparison always true.
_checks.memory: Peak RSS exceeded the runner budget.
_checks.type2_gate_liveness: A large same-shape population was demoted and not one visible cluster reached `nearly_identical` through the gate's own saturating-shape precondition ([FUSED-CONTENT-GATE]). A population-shape heuristic, not a recall assertion: it identifies no expected pair. `identical` does not count (decided by byte equivalence before the gate runs) and neither does a sub-floor token near-miss (classified by the ordinary Type-3 path without the gate judging it).
_checks.type2_recall: A hand-verified Type-2 rename curated in the manifest's `must_find_type2` was not reported as a shown cluster spanning its files at the entry's curated `min_nodes` extent and within its optional `max_rank` ceiling. A hidden occurrence on either curated side is a miss, so is a spanning cluster below the extent floor, and so is the curated duplicate buried past its ceiling - a boilerplate family or fragment touching both paths is not the curated duplicate (gh #439). The rank clause is judged on the cluster that reaches the extent floor, never on the first cluster touching both paths. An entry curating no `min_nodes` fails rather than passing on a path overlap. The engine must also have vouched for the pair: admitted, content guard satisfied where its route requires one, and classified `nearly_identical`. That verdict is not on the cluster - the mass-only wire keeps evidence off components - so the gate asks for it through `deslop --compare`, and an entry with no verdict fails rather than passing on a measurement never taken (gh #488). Recall is what the report shows, not what it contains — a false negative on known rename ground truth ([CORPUS-RECALL]).
_checks.files_analysed: [CORPUS-SCOPE] The scan analysed fewer files than the manifest's `expect_files_min` floor, or the manifest curates no floor at all. A scan that reached zero files renders clean, exits 0 and satisfies every other check in this suite, because each of them iterates a set that is empty (gh #342).
_checks.cluster_count_band: [CORPUS-SCOPE] The rendered cluster count fell outside the manifest's `expect_clusters` band. Below it, detection stopped finding duplicates; above it, something started manufacturing them - repository-wide swings no per-cluster check can see.
